logline: A teenager moves to Ikebukuro seeking excitement and finds himself entangled with a headless dullahan courier, a manipulative information broker, and an underground gang whose members do not know each other - a city as a web of secrets pulling tighter.

renewal.note: The anime adaptation concluded with Durarara!!x2 Ketsu in March 2016, covering the full light novel run. No further continuation planned.

bollymeter.basis: MAL score of 8.09 from 692,523 users; widely praised for its multi-perspective narrative structure and ensemble character writing, with particular acclaim for the Celty Sturluson storyline and the series' Ikebukuro world-building.

seasons.review_body: Durarara!! arrived in January 2010 and distinguished itself through structural ambition: rather than following a single protagonist, it rotated perspectives across roughly eleven recurring characters whose storylines only gradually revealed their intersections. Brain's Base adapted Ryohgo Narita's light novel with an energy calibrated to Ikebukuro's density - each episode layering a new angle on the same urban space until the city itself became a character. The headless courier Celty Sturluson anchors the series' mythological underpinning without overwhelming the grounded gang dynamics; her story generates some of the highest-scoring episode discussions in the MAL thread record. The MAL score of 8.09 from nearly 700,000 users places it solidly in the upper tier of its era's urban fantasy anime. The show rewards attentive viewing: relationships introduced casually in episode two carry weight in episode twenty.

episode_reviews.title: Exit 1: A Newbie's Perspective
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces Ikebukuro through the eyes of Mikado Ryugamine, newly arrived from a small town and narrating the city's strangeness with the wonder of someone who asked for exactly this. Shizuo hurling a vending machine and Celty riding silently through traffic establish the register fast: this city is not normal and does not apologize for it.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The headless rider materializes through Ikebukuro traffic in the first episode, the show's clearest signal that Durarara operates on supernatural terms without explanation or apology.

episode_reviews.title: Heaven's Vengeance Is Slow but Sure
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint episode is where the show's multi-perspective structure clicks: the same event is shown from three angles and each retelling reveals a character layer the previous one concealed. The pivot from ensemble introduction to converging crisis begins here.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Izaya's manipulation of events is revealed to have been operating in plain sight since the first episode - visible only in retrospect.

bollymeter.basis: The three-cour second season (x2 Shou, Ten, Ketsu) was received positively by fans of the first season but noted for pacing issues as it stretched to cover the novel's more complex gang-war arcs across 36 episodes.

seasons.review_body: The second season - broadcast across three cours as Durarara!!x2 Shou (January 2015), x2 Ten (July 2015), and x2 Ketsu (January 2016) - was produced by Shuka after Brain's Base did not continue, with most of the creative staff intact. The transition showed: the character relationships and ensemble interplay maintained the first season's quality, but the extended gang-war narrative introduced through x2 Ten and Ketsu strained pacing across 36 episodes. Audience reception was warmer among fans already invested in the cast than among newcomers. The finale resolved character arcs that the first season left deliberately open. As a complete work, the second season functions as the necessary conclusion to the Narita adaptation rather than a standalone season, and fans of the first season generally found it worthwhile.
seasons.season_over_season: The second season shifts from urban-mystery ensemble to a full gang-war saga, gaining closure but losing some of the first season's compact energy across its expanded 36-episode run.
